title: Migrate probe taxonomy + sampling ontology to eval-harness (and refresh defaults for 2026H1)
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Docs-only: eval-harness now contains the canonical probe taxonomy + sampling ontology, plus a probes-v3 schema note and updated quota defaults for 2026H1.
description:
Context: The probe taxonomy + sampling ontology doc currently lives in Confluence (applied-ml-and-evals/prompt-sets-and-benchmarks/workload-probe-taxonomy-and-sampling-ontology-2026) and has been increasingly out of sync with what eval-harness actually enforces (category naming, retention defaults, and the priority bump API semantics). This PR migrates the document into eval-harness so the docs and code live together, and refreshes a small set of defaults to match 2026H1 behavior.

What changed (high level): Migrated the Confluence doc into eval-harness under docs/workload-probes/workload-probe-taxonomy-and-sampling-ontology.md and added a short front-matter block describing ownership + review cadence. Updated a few facts that had drifted: (1) category naming: we standardize on latency_tail (instead of lat-tail) in configs, while still accepting lat-tail as an alias in catalogs for back-compat; (2) anchor reservation: anchors are still reserved (not charged against the daily budget) but the default reserve_anchors is now 8 (was 5) to cover the expanded daily smoke+drift suite; (3) quota defaults: small re-balance based on Jan–Mar utilization (functioncall down slightly, multimodal up slightly, latency_tail up slightly); (4) sampling algorithm guidance: clarified when to use deterministic stratified reservoir vs. weighted round robin, and documented the tie-breaker order to make selection reproducible across languages; (5) schema note: doc now references probes-v3.yaml (renamed from probes-v2.yaml) and clarifies that cost_estimate_tokens is stored as an integer, while NDJSON export remains stringly typed for historical reasons.

Updated defaults (2026H1): Default budget example remains 10,000 probe calls/day. Default quota weights now: smoke 1%, slice_coverage 58% (was 60%), longtail 10% (unchanged), latency_tail 10% (was 8%), quant_stress 6% (unchanged), multimodal 4% (was 3%), functioncall 11% (was 12%). Anchor reservation default now 8 (was 5).

Priority scoring clarification: Kept the same conceptual formula S = base * (1 + p_team + p_risk + p_recency), but clarified that p_recency is capped at 1.2 (previously described as 0.0–1.0 without an explicit cap and the implementation effectively capped at ~1.2). Added a note that emergency bumps via priority-bump API are rate-limited per slice per 24h and require an incident or customer escalation reference.

Retention policy defaults: Kept the same category list and spirit, but updated two defaults to match the stewardship policy enacted in February: smoke retention is now 21d (was 30d), latency_tail retention is now 45d (was 60d). Everything else unchanged unless a business justification extends it.

Operational checklist: No major changes; tightened a few steps to match current gates: the onboarding checklist now requires at least 5 gold-labeled anchors per new probe family (was 3) and requires a probe-checker validate run against probes-v3.yaml. The promotion criteria now references <1.5% slice fidelity delta (was <2%) because that is what regression triage uses for paging thresholds.

Why this belongs in eval-harness: This doc drives how people write sampler configs and how we reason about expected selection composition. Keeping it near sampler code + schema reduces drift and makes changes reviewable via normal PR processes.

Follow-ups (out of scope here): (a) Remove lat-tail alias in 2026Q3 after remaining catalogs are migrated. (b) Add a small script to render the quota table in the doc from the default config struct to prevent divergence.

Testing/validation: Docs build (mkdocs) + link checker; ran probe-checker validate against a handful of existing catalogs to confirm the probes-v3 pointer is correct; verified that sampler config examples match current field names (latency_tail, quant_stress, slice_coverage).

review_conversation:
Arjun Patel (review): Can we be explicit about the lat-tail alias behavior? People have configs in the wild that still say lat-tail. Also please call out the p_recency cap: the implementation is 1.2 today and we should match it. Maya Chen (author): Added an alias note: latency_tail is canonical in configs; catalogs may still store lat-tail during migration. Also updated the p_recency section with a 1.2 cap and a note about rate limiting.

Elena Rossi (review): Quota change rationale looks reasonable but can you link to the utilization dashboard? Also small nit: the doc says cost_estimate_tokens integer but the NDJSON example uses a string. Maya Chen (author): Added a pointer to the internal dashboard (Metrics > Eval Sampler > Category Utilization Jan–Mar 2026) and added a compatibility note explaining the NDJSON export is stringly typed.

Diego Marquez (review): Retention defaults: are we sure about latency_tail 45d? I recall infra policy reduced it due to storage. Priya Nair (review): Confirmed with stewardship: 45d is correct as of 2026-02-27; 60d was pre-policy. Maya Chen (author): Updated retention table and added a short note that defaults can be extended with justification + reviewer sign-off.

Priya Nair (review): Please update onboarding step from 3 anchors to 5 anchors; QA has been rejecting new families that don’t meet 5. Maya Chen (author): Done; also tightened promotion threshold to <1.5% fidelity delta to match paging rubric.

Arjun Patel (approval): LGTM after latest edits. Elena Rossi (approval): Approved. Diego Marquez (approval): Approved.
